title: Passing to the schematic closure
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S$ be any compactification
([sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]) with $\overline X$ Noetherian, and let
$i:Z\hookrightarrow\overline X$ be the schematic closure of $X$, with
$j_Z:X\hookrightarrow Z$ the induced open immersion
([sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure]). For a condensed coefficient ring
$\Lambda$, use its pulled-back coefficient sheaves on these schemes. For
every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\Lambda_X)$ there are canonical
identifications, in $D(\overline X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\Lambda_{\overline X})$
and $D(S_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\Lambda_S)$ respectively,

$$
j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K,\qquad
Rp_*j_!K\simeq R(p\circ i)_*j_{Z,!}K.
$$

Thus, for schemes of finite type over $k$, replacing a compactification by
the schematic closure of $X$ does not change the expression $Rp_*j_!$
defining $Rf_!$; that expression needs only an open immersion followed by a
proper morphism.

proof.text:
By [det-nagata-density-normalization-setup], the given compactification and its schematic closure satisfy the comparison setup: $j=i\circ j_Z$, $j_Z$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, and $V=\overline X\setminus Z$ is a quasi-compact open with closed complement $Z$. The same setup says that $\overline X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus clause (2) of [det-sf-open-closed-pullback-limits], with $B=\Lambda_{\overline X}$, makes the closed restriction $i^*$ exact for these coefficients. In particular it sends an acyclic complex to an acyclic complex: exactness preserves kernels and images, so $H^n(i^*C)=i^*H^n(C)=0$. Hence the closed restriction occurring in the sheaf comparison is computed degreewise on the unbounded derived category, as used in the source's first paragraph. Apply the unbounded-complex clause of [det-nagata-density-normalization-sheaves] to the pulled-back coefficient sheaves and any complex representing the given $K$. It supplies the canonical identification in $D(\overline X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\Lambda_{\overline X})$:

$$j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K.$$

The cited clause explicitly induces this identification in the derived category.

Apply [det-nagata-density-normalization-pushforward] to these compactification, closure, and coefficient data. It gives the canonical identification in $D(S_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\Lambda_S)$:

$$Rp_*j_!K\simeq R(p\circ i)_*j_{Z,!}K.$$

Parts (1) and (4) of [det-nagata-density-normalization-setup] say that $j_Z$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and $p\circ i$ is proper. Also $(p\circ i)\circ j_Z=p\circ j=f$. Hence $X\xrightarrow{j_Z}Z\xrightarrow{p\circ i}S$ is a compactification by [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. Its compact-support expression is $R(p\circ i)_*j_{Z,!}$, whereas the original expression is $Rp_*j_!$. The displayed natural identification equates these expressions, proving the final assertion, in particular for finite-type $k$-schemes.
